Files Amended 2025 Annual Financial Statements and MD&A.

Varennes, Quebec, November 13, 2026 – TheNewswire - CHARBONE CORPORATION (TSXV: CH; OTCQB: CHHYF; FSE: K47) (“CHARBONE” or the “Company”), a vertically integrated industrial gases company focused on production, distribution and storage of clean ultra-high purity (“UHP”) hydrogen and other strategic industrial gases, today announces the filing of its 2025 Amended Consolidated Financial Statements and Management’s Discussion & Analysis, as well as the corresponding officers’ certificates, in connection with a routine continuous disclosure review conducted by staff at the Autorité des marchés financiers (“AMF”). The correction does not have any impact on operating loss nor the Company’s cash flows.

 

During the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, the Company agreed with certain suppliers to settle trade payables through the issuance of units. Each unit represented either one common share of the Company or one common share and one warrant of the Company. During the third quarter of 2026, following a review of the accounting treatment applied to these transactions, the Company concluded that certain gains on settlement of accounts payable had been incorrectly measured. The error of accounting entry has been corrected by restating the amounts recognized for the year ended December 31, 2025 to reflect the measurement of the equity instruments incorporating quoted prices in active market at the date the securities were issued and not at the time and conditions the Company concluded these transactions with some suppliers.

 

AMENDED 2025 IMPACTS:

  • Share capital and warrants amounts increased respectively by $1 million and $0.7 million with a net impact of nil on shareholder equity. 

  • No impact on total assets nor total liabilities. 

  • For the year ending December 31, 2025, the financial expense has increased by $1.7 million without any impact on operating loss nor the Company’s cash flows. 

“The correction is primarily linked to the appreciation of the share price between the negotiation of the suppliers’ settlement agreement occurred in 2025 and the issuance of the shares and management understands and agrees with the highly technical accounting treatment point of view articulated by the AMF,” said Benoit Veilleux, Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary of CHARBONE. “CHARBONE will continue to take the regulator’s comments very seriously and has demonstrated its good faith throughout its discussions with staff members to explain the basis for its financial reporting.” 

The Company has provided corrective disclosure in the amended annual filings to address the matters described above. The Company is also continuously enhancing its disclosure controls and procedures, including its processes for preparing and reviewing financial reporting.

TORONTO, ON / ACCESS Newswire / November 13, 2026 / Grid Metals Corp. (TSXV:GRDM)(OTCQB:MSMGF) ("Grid" or the "Company") has filed on SEDAR+ the independent technical report (the "Report") supporting the Mineral Resource Estimate ("MRE") for its 85%-owned Falcon West Cesium Property ("Falcon West" or the "Property") located in southeastern Manitoba, Canada. The MRE has an effective date of September 25, 2026, and was prepared in accordance with the Canadian Securities Administrators' National Instrument 43-101 - Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects ("NI 43-101"). There are no material differences in the Report from the results disclosed in the Company's news release dated September 30, 2026. The Report is titled "Technical Report on the Mineral Resource Estimate for the Lucy South Cesium Deposit, Falcon West Project, Municipality of Reynolds, Manitoba, Canada" and was prepared by SGS Canada Inc. The Report can be found under the Company's issuer profile on SEDAR+ (www.sedarplus.com).

Investors Relations Agreement with Peterson Capital

In addition to the consulting fees outlined to Peterson Capital in Grid's September 8, 2026 press release, Peterson Capital also received a C$5,000 expense deposit to cover anticipated marketing expenses associated with its investor outreach activities. The deposit is separate from the consulting fees disclosed in the aforementioned press release and is subject to reconciliation against actual expenses incurred.

About Cesium and the Cesium Market

Cesium is the heaviest stable alkali metal with a unique set of characteristics due to its position on the periodic table. It is highly reactive, has excellent photoelectric properties, and has a large ionic radius. It is the metal of choice across a number of applications, including atomic clocks, 5G infrastructure, defence targeting optics, and next-generation green tech.

Cesium is defined as a critical metal by both Canada and the U.S owing to its supply chain vulnerability. There is currently believed to be a significant shortage of cesium feedstock globally1. The industry revolves around extreme supply concentration with the United States and several European allies being 100% net import reliant for their cesium needs1. Pollucite has historically been the mineral of choice for cesium extraction given its high cesium content.

About Lucy South

  • The Lucy South cesium deposit contains an open pit measured resource for the Lithium-Cesium-Tantalum ("LCT") Zone of 51,500 tonnes at 2.58% Cs2O and 1.47% Li2O2; the LCT Zone encloses a higher-grade cesium-rich Pollucite Zone containing a measured resource of 15,600 tonnes at 5.19% Cs2O and 1.76% Li2O.
    • Total contained metal in the measured category of 1,322 tonnes Cs2O.
  • This resource is believed to be the second largest cesium resource in active development in the western world3.
  • The resource is contained within a highly-fractionated LCT pegmatite, the Lucy South pegmatite, and covers an area of ~120 metres by ~50 metres and has an average depth from surface of ~20 metres.
  • It is located 130 km east of Winnipeg and 500 metres north of the TransCanada Highway. It is proximal to the intra-continental railway system and Manitoba's low-cost hydro-electric power grid.
  • The resource is partly open along strike and down dip.

About Falcon West

  • The focus of the Falcon West joint venture between Grid (85%) and Avenir (15%) is to establish a producing cesium operation at the Lucy South cesium zone. Cesium is a rare critical metal with a number of forward-facing industrial uses. The scope of the project is to establish a small footprint operation that uses crushing and XRT ore sorting (no water utilized or extensive infrastructure) in the production of a cesium-bearing pollucite concentrate to be sold to downstream cesium chemical producers.
  • Falcon West consists of 124 unpatented mining claims located 130 km east of Winnipeg and is transected by the Trans Canada Highway. Most of Grid's exploration efforts have focused on the Lucy claims in the northeastern part of the property.
  • Exploration potential in the project area remains high with a number of occurrences of spodumene and pollucite mineralization noted in the immediate project area (the Artdon-Lucy target area) that extends for >1 km along strike and >500 metres across strike. Of note is a large gap in historical drilling between the Artdon LCT pegmatite occurrence in the west and the Lucy South and Lucy North LCT pegmatites in the east.
  • The Company is also eying the potential for outlining additional cesium resources in the project area. Drilling is expected to commence in January 2027 focused on expansion of the Lucy South resource and identifying new LCT pegmatites with cesium potential. A strong magnetic low anomaly interpreted to reflect a large volume of near surface granitic pegmatite coincides with the Artdon-Lucy pegmatite trend and extends several km along strike in both directions.

Quality Assurance and Quality Control

The Company's ongoing exploration program at the Falcon West cesium/lithium property is being supervised by Dave Peck, P.Geo. Grid Metals applies best practice quality assurance and quality control ("QAQC") protocols on all of its exploration programs. For the current program, all core was logged and sampled at the Company's core facility located on its Makwa nickel property. Generally, 1.0 metre sample lengths were used. Samples were bagged and tagged and then transported by secure carrier to the Activation Laboratories facility in Ancaster, Ontario for sample preparation and analysis for lithium, cesium, rubidium, tantalum and selected major and trace element abundances using a sodium peroxide fusion total digestion method followed by ICP-OES and ICP-MS analysis. The Company is using two rare metal certified reference materials ("CRMs") and an analytical blank for the program to monitor analytical accuracy and check for cross contamination between samples. The blank and CRM results for the reported intervals were determined to fall within the accepted range of deviation from the certified values. A check assay program using a similar sodium peroxide fusion digestion method has recently been initiated with check samples being analyzed at AGAT Laboratories in Thunder Bay, Ontario.

Qualified Person Statement

The Mineral Resource Estimate (MRE) was prepared by Rohan Millar, P.Geo., of SGS Geological Services in accordance with the 2014 Canadian Institute of Mining, Metallurgy and Petroleum Definition Standards and Canadian National Instrument 43-101 ("NI 43-101"). Mr. Millar is an independent Qualified Person as defined by NI 43-101 and has reviewed and approved the contents of this news release.

Dr. Dave Peck, P.Geo., is a Qualified Person as defined in National Instrument 43-101 - Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects ("NI 43-101") and has reviewed and approved the scientific and technical information disclosed in this release. Dr. Peck is not independent of the Company within the meaning of NI 43-101 as he is an officer of Grid.

About Grid Metals Corp.

The Company is one of the largest mineral rights holders in the Province of Manitoba with over 250,000 hectares of mineral claims and exploration licenses registered to Grid. The current focus of Grid is its Falcon West Property which is advancing towards commercial production following the release of a maiden cesium resource at the Lucy South deposit. A summary of Grid's mineral properties in Manitoba include:

  1. The Falcon West Property (Li-Cs) is located 130 km east of Winnipeg along the Trans-Canada highway and contains an open pit measured mineral resource at the Lucy South deposit of 51,500 tonnes grading 2.58% Cs2O and 1.47% Li2O2. The property is subject to a joint venture agreement with Avenir, which has a 15% interest in the property.
  2. The Makwa Property (Ni-Cu-PGM-Co), which is subject to an Option and Joint Venture Agreement with Teck Resources Limited ("Teck"). Teck can earn up to a 70% interest in Makwa by incurring a total of C$17.3 million, comprising project expenditures (C$15.7 million) and cash payments or equity participation (C$1.6 million) with Grid. Makwa is located on the south arm of the Bird River Greenstone Belt and contains an open pit indicated mineral resource of 14.2 million tonnes grading 0.48% nickel, 0.11% copper, and 0.37 g/t palladium4.
  3. The Mayville Property (Cu-Ni) is located on the north arm of the Bird River Greenstone Belt. Grid owns a cumulative 89% interest in the project. The project contains an open pit indicated mineral resource of 32.0 million tonnes grading 0.40% copper, 0.16% nickel, and 0.13 g/t palladium4.
  4. The Donner Property (Li-Cs) is adjacent to the Mayville Property, and Grid owns 75% of the project. The project contains an open pit inferred mineral resource of 2.1 million tonnes grading 1.42% Li2O and an underground inferred mineral resource of 4.7 million tonnes grading 1.37% Li2O5.
  5. The Thompson East (Cu-Ni-PGM) Property is located east of the city of Thompson in north-central Manitoba and captures a number of high tenor Cu- and PGE-rich magmatic sulphide occurrences that are interpreted to be related to the development of the adjacent Thompson Nickel Belt. The property is subject to an Option and Joint Venture Agreement with Boliden Mineral Canada Ltd ("Boliden"). Boliden is currently sole-funding early-stage exploration on the property.
  6. The 100%-owned Fox River (Cu-Ni-PGM-Au) Property located in the Gillam region of northeastern Manitoba and covering 90 km of strike of the highly prospective Fox River Belt - a direct analogue to the Raglan nickel district in northern Quebec.

All of the Company's southeastern Manitoba projects are located on the ancestral lands of the Sagkeeng First Nation with whom the Company maintains an Exploration Agreement.

References Cited:

  1. US Geological Survey Mineral Commodity Summaries - Cesium - February 2026.
  2. NI 43-101 report by SGS Canada dated September 25, 2026 and entitled ‘Technical Report on the Mineral Resource Estimate for the Lucy South Cesium Deposit, Falcon West Project, Municipality of Reynolds, Manitoba, Canada.
  3. Power Metals Corp and PMET Resources are actively developing pollucite-bearing cesium projects. Power Metals' Case Lake project has an open pit inferred mineral resource of 13,000 tonnes at 2.4% Cs2O and 1.3% Li2O. PMET's Shaakichiuwaanaan project has open pit resources across two zones (Rigel and Vega) hosted within the open pit resource of its CV13 pegmatite.
  4. NI 43-101 report by Micon International dated June 14, 2024 and entitled ‘NI 43-101 Technical Report on the Updated Mineral Resources Estimate of the Makwa-Mayville (MM) Project, Manitoba, Canada.
  5. NI 43-101 report by SGS Geological Services dated September 1, 2023 and entitled ‘Technical Report on a Mineral Resource Estimate for the Donner Lake Lithium Property, Manitoba, Canada.

–First Quarter Revenue Increased 27% Year-over-Year to $5.4 Million; Revenue Plus Interest Income of $5.9 Million*–

–Revenue from Sources Other Than Commissions Rose to 68% of Total Revenue, from 45%–

–AtlasClearing Net Capital Increased to $15.2 Million, $14.9 Million in Excess of Requirements–

–Definitive Agreement to Acquire Ark Financial Services Signed and FINRA Continuing Membership Application Filed; Correspondent Network Expanded to Nine Signed Agreements–

–Earnings Conference Call Scheduled for Monday, November 16, 2026, at 8:30 AM ET–

TAMPA, Fla., Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AtlasClear Holdings, Inc. (“AtlasClear” or the “Company”) (ATCH), a company building regulated financial infrastructure for smaller institutions, fintechs and advisors, today announced financial results for its fiscal first quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Fiscal First Quarter 2027 Financial Highlights

(Quarter Ended September 30, 2026)

  • Revenue increased 27% year-over-year to $5.4 million, compared to $4.3 million in the prior-year quarter.
  • Revenue plus interest income increased 24% to $5.9 million, compared to $4.7 million in the prior-year quarter.*
  • Revenue from sources other than commissions represented approximately 68% of total revenue, compared to approximately 45% in the prior-year quarter, reflecting continued diversification of the revenue base.
  • AtlasClearing’s net capital increased to $15.2 million at September 30, 2026, from $14.4 million at June 30, 2026, and was $14.9 million in excess of its minimum requirement, well above the $10 million excess net capital threshold the National Securities Clearing Corporation requires of firms that clear for introducing brokers.
  • Stockholders’ equity was $20.7 million at September 30, 2026.
  • Cash and cash equivalents totaled $9.4 million; total cash including segregated customer and PAB reserve cash totaled approximately $35.8 million.
  • Net loss was $1.1 million, or $(0.01) per share, compared to a net loss of $0.4 million, or $(0.01) per share, in the prior-year quarter. Operating expenses included approximately $1.3 million in regulatory, legal and professional fees, driven by the planned Ark Financial Services and Commercial Bancorp transactions, and $0.6 million in non-cash stock-based compensation.

*This is a non-GAAP financial measure; see below for additional information.

  • Compensation, payroll taxes and benefits expense declined 13% year-over-year to $2.7 million, while revenue grew 27%.

Management Commentary

“We are building exactly the business we set out to build, and this quarter shows it,” said John Schaible, Executive Chairman of AtlasClear Holdings. “Revenue grew 27%, we built stock locate into our largest revenue line, and AtlasClearing’s net capital rose to $15.2 million. And we grew revenue while compensation costs fell 13%, which tells us that not every new dollar of revenue requires more people. We delivered that growth before our newly signed correspondents made any material contribution, which gives us confidence in the opportunity ahead. I know the recent trading suspension has been difficult for our shareholders, and we take that seriously. The Exchange’s action is about our share price. It is not about AtlasClearing’s regulatory capital, the Company’s financial condition or our operations. We intend to pursue the appeal process and seek to restore trading on the NYSE American, and we intend to seek to effect a reverse stock split as part of our plan to support the appeal and our continued listing. But the share price is not the business. The business is growing, the team is executing, and nothing about our foundation has changed.”

“Stock locate is the clearest proof of what this platform can do,” said Craig Ridenhour, President of AtlasClear Holdings and Chairman of AtlasClearing, Inc. “A year ago it did not exist, and this quarter it generated $3.0 million, more than any other part of our business. That is what happens when you add a new service to infrastructure that is already built and well capitalized. Now we are doing the same thing with correspondents. Every firm we bring through onboarding adds accounts and trading activity to an engine that already earns revenue across commissions, clearing, stock locate and interest, and we expect to support much of that growth with the platform and team already in place. My team is in that work every day, and none of it has slowed down.”

Operational and Strategic Highlights

During and following the quarter, AtlasClear continued executing on its strategy to build an integrated financial services platform combining clearing, capital markets and banking capabilities. Key developments included:

  • In October 2026, signed a definitive business combination agreement to acquire Ark Financial Services, Inc., the parent of Dawson James Securities, Inc., and completed an initial 24.9% investment funded with $2.5 million in cash and a $2.5 million seller note, with no AtlasClear shares issued. Dawson James, an active underwriter and placement agent that already clears through AtlasClearing, reported 2025 revenue of $25.1 million and audited net income of $2.4 million. Because Ark’s principal serves on the Company’s board of directors, the transaction was reviewed and approved by AtlasClear’s independent directors.
  • On November 12, 2026, the continuing membership application for Dawson James was filed with FINRA. FINRA approval is the principal regulatory condition to the acquisition of the remaining 75.1% of Ark, which also remains subject to stockholder approval to the extent required and other customary closing conditions. The remaining consideration will be paid solely in cash and AtlasClear common stock, with no warrants, preferred stock, convertible securities, discounts or price resets, and Ark stockholders receiving AtlasClear shares will be subject to a six-month lock-up.
  • Expanded AtlasClearing’s correspondent network to nine signed correspondent broker-dealer agreements, four of which were signed since the start of fiscal 2027, with onboarding and conversion under way.

Key Terms

triple net leasefinancial
A triple net lease is a rental agreement where the tenant pays the base rent plus three main ongoing costs: property taxes, building insurance, and routine maintenance. For investors, this shifts much of the expense and risk onto the tenant, creating a steadier, more predictable income stream for the property owner—similar to renting a furnished home where the renter also pays the bills—making valuation and cash-flow forecasting simpler.
reitfinancial
A real estate investment trust (REIT) is a company that owns, operates, or finances income-producing real estate, like shopping centers, apartments, or office buildings. For investors, REITs offer a way to invest in real estate without having to buy property directly, often providing regular income through dividends. They function like a mutual fund for real estate, making it easier for people to add property investments to their portfolio.
ebitdafinancial
EBITDA stands for earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization. It measures a company's profitability by focusing on the money it makes from its core operations, ignoring expenses like taxes and accounting adjustments. Investors use EBITDA to compare how well different companies are performing financially, as it provides a clearer picture of operational success without the influence of financial structure or accounting choices.

adjusted ebitdafinancial
Adjusted EBITDA is a way companies measure how much money they make from their core operations, like running a business, by removing certain costs or income that aren’t part of regular business activities. It helps investors see how well a company is doing without distractions from unusual expenses or gains, making it easier to compare companies or track performance over time.

BRISBANE, Calif., Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Tempest Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: TPST) (“Tempest”), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing a pipeline of advanced in vivo chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (“CAR-T”) product candidates to treat cancer and autoimmune disease, today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provided a business update.

“The third quarter marked a period of meaningful progress in the advancement of two next-generation in vivo CAR-T platforms with the potential to transform treatment across multiple diseases,” said Matt Angel, Ph.D., president and chief executive officer of Tempest. “We made important strides in expanding our pipeline and strengthening our position in the rapidly evolving in vivo CAR-T landscape through our strategic collaboration with Senlang by obtaining exclusive license rights to our clinical-stage BCMA/GPRC5D in vivo CAR-T candidate TPST-4903, while securing access to additional capital to support our development priorities. We also welcomed two accomplished independent directors to our Board, bringing valuable corporate governance and capital markets expertise as we navigate our next phase of growth. Together, these achievements reinforce our commitment to advancing our pipeline, executing on our strategic priorities and unlocking the broad therapeutic potential of in vivo CAR-T therapies for patients.”

Recent Highlights

  • TPST-4903
    • Exercised option under agreement with Hebei Senlang Biotechnology Co., Ltd. to obtain an exclusive license to develop and commercialize Senlang’s CD7-targeted lentiviral vector platform and associated in vivo CAR-T candidates worldwide, excluding China.
    • The lead program, TPST-4903, is a BCMA/GPRC5D dual-targeting in vivo CAR-T candidate being evaluated in a Phase 1 dose-escalation study in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (rrMM). The initial data demonstrating encouraging preliminary clinical responses are expected to be presented at an upcoming scientific conference.

  • TPST-4003

    • Unveiled next-generation in vivo CAR-T pipeline, including lead product candidate TPST-4003, a dual-targeting CD19/BCMA in vivo CAR-T candidate that combines the Company’s proprietary CD7-targeted mRNA/LNP delivery with its clinically validated dual-target CAR architecture for broad B-cell lineage depletion and reset.
    • Executed a strategic partnership in July 2026 with Hebei Senlang Biotechnology to collaborate on the development of certain of Tempest’s proprietary in vivo CAR-T product candidates, including the Company’s next-generation CD7-targeted TPST-4003. An investigator-initiated trial in China evaluating TPST-4003 in approximately 10 patients with myasthenia gravis or multiple sclerosis is expected to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026.

  • Corporate:

    • Completed a private placement in September 2026 of pre-funded warrants and Series C and D warrants for gross proceeds of approximately $2.5 million (approximately $1.8 million net of placement agent fees and offering expenses), excluding up to approximately $5.0 million of gross proceeds that may be received upon the cash exercise of the Series C and D warrants.
    • Entered into a purchase agreement with Lincoln Park Capital Fund, LLC on August 13, 2026 that gives Tempest the right, but not the obligation, to sell up to $25.0 million of its common stock, increasing to $50.0 million if the initial amount is sold, over a 24-month period that began September 1, 2026.Through September 30, 2026, Tempest sold 350,000 shares to Lincoln Park for gross proceeds of approximately $0.3 million.
    • Strengthened Board of Directors with the appointments of independent directors, Nancy Freda-Smith and John W. Frederick boosting corporate governance and capital markets expertise.

Financial Results

Third Quarter 2026

  • Tempest ended the quarter with $0.9 million in cash and cash equivalents, compared to $7.7 million on December 31, 2025. The decrease was primarily due to cash used in operations, including one-time transaction-associated costs incurred prior to or upon closing of the Asset Acquisition in February 2026, offset by the net proceeds from the Company’s private placement of common stock and warrants in March 2026 of $1.7 million, the warrant inducement in May 2026 of $1.7 million, sales of common stock under the Lincoln Park equity line of credit of $0.3 million and the Company’s private placement in September 2026 of $1.8 million. The Company’s existing cash and cash equivalents are expected to fund its projected operating expense requirements for less than 12 months from the date the financial statements were available to be issued, and there is substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern.
  • Net loss and net loss per share for the quarter were $3.6 million and $0.21, respectively, compared to $3.5 million and $0.79, respectively, for the three months ended September 30, 2025.
  • Research and development expenses for the quarter were $0.2 million compared to $0.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The $0.4 million decrease was primarily due to a decrease in costs incurred as a result of the portfolio re-prioritization after the Asset Acquisition in February 2026, offset by research and manufacturing costs related to the Company’s CAR-T product candidates.
  • General and administrative expenses for the quarter were $2.6 million compared to $3.0 million for the same period in 2025. The $0.4 million decrease was primarily due to a decrease in one-time separation and other costs incurred in the third quarter of 2025, offset by other administrative expenses.
  • Financing costs related to the Lincoln Park equity line of credit for the quarter were $0.8 million, consisting of $0.66 million for the fair value of the commitment shares issued to Lincoln Park and $0.15 million of issuance costs, net of a nominal gain on shares sold to Lincoln Park. There were no financing costs in the three months ended September 30, 2025.

Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026

  • Cash used in operating activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $12.4 million.
  • Net loss and net loss per share for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 were $36.6 million and $2.54, respectively, compared to $22.2 million and $5.71, respectively, for the same period in 2025.
  • Research and development expenses for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 were $2.1 million, compared to $12.1 million for the same period in 2025. The $9.9 million decrease was primarily due to a decrease in costs incurred as a result of re-prioritizing efforts towards exploring strategic alternatives initiated in April 2025 and resulting in the Asset Acquisition completed in February 2026.
  • General and administrative expenses for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 were $11.5 million, compared to $10.4 million for the same period in 2025. The $1.0 million increase was primarily due to one-time costs resulting from the Asset Acquisition completed in February 2026.
  • Acquired in-process research and development expenses for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 were $22.2 million compared to nil for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Costs incurred prior to or upon closing the Asset Acquisition in the prior three months ended March 31, 2026 were expensed as acquired in-process research and development.
  • Financing costs related to the Lincoln Park equity line of credit for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 were $0.8 million, all of which were recognized in the third quarter of 2026. There were no financing costs in the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

About Tempest Therapeutics

Tempest is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing a pipeline of advanced in vivo CAR-T therapies designed to treat cancer and autoimmune disease by resetting dysfunctional immunity. Tempest’s portfolio includes TPST-4903, a BCMA/GPRC5D dual-targeting in vivo CAR-T candidate being evaluated in a Phase 1 study for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (rrMM). The Company’s lead lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based in vivo CAR-T candidate, TPST-4003 combines a clinically supported dual-targeting CD19/BCMA CAR structure with an advanced CD7-targeting delivery platform to support broad immune reset across multiple indications. The company’s additional preclinical programs leverage advanced payloads to create a modular in vivo CAR-T portfolio. Tempest envisions a world in which immune reset therapies bring safe, effective, and broadly accessible therapeutic options to patients in need. Key Terms

long-term capital gainsfinancial
Profit realized when an investor sells an asset they have owned longer than the legally specified holding period; these gains are taxed under “long-term” rules that typically carry lower tax rates than gains on assets sold quickly. It matters to investors because lower tax rates increase the amount of money they keep after a sale, so holding an investment longer can be like letting a high-interest coupon compound before withdrawing the cash, affecting decisions about when to sell and overall portfolio returns.
View in glossary
qualified dividendsfinancial
Dividends that meet tax rules allowing them to be taxed at the lower long-term capital gains rates instead of higher ordinary income rates. For investors, that means more of the payment stays in your pocket; it influences which dividend-paying stocks you buy and how long you hold them, similar to getting a discount for meeting a store’s membership conditions.
closed-end investment companyfinancial
A closed-end investment company is a pooled investment fund that issues a fixed number of shares in a one-time offering and then has those shares bought and sold on an exchange like a stock; a professional manager runs the portfolio of assets. It matters to investors because the market price can move above or below the value of the underlying holdings, affecting returns and income, and shares may be less flexible to issue or redeem compared with open-ended funds—think of buying a slice of a privately baked pie whose market price can differ from the pie’s actual ingredients value.

Manufacturing Work Addressing FDA CMC Information Requests Substantially Completed

NDA Resubmission Expected Between December 2026 and January 2027

KANSAS CITY, Kan., Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Cingulate Inc. (NASDAQ: CING), a biopharmaceutical company utilizing its proprietary Precision Timed Release™ (PTR™) drug delivery platform to develop a pipeline of next-generation products, today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and announced that it has substantially completed the manufacturing work required to address the U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s (FDA) chemistry, manufacturing and controls (CMC) information requests for CTx-1301. The Company expects to resubmit the new drug application (NDA) for CTx-1301 between December 2026 and January 2027.

“With the manufacturing work substantially complete, we are now finalizing the data and documentation needed to resubmit the NDA for CTx-1301, and we expect to do so by January 2027, potentially sooner,” stated Cingulate Chairman and CEO Shane J. Schaffer. “Importantly, the FDA’s Complete Response Letter did not raise any concerns about the clinical safety or efficacy of CTx-1301. We thank our shareholders for their patience and continued support as we work to bring this treatment to patients with ADHD.”

Regulatory Update: CTx-1301 NDA Resubmission Progress

On June 1, 2026, the FDA issued a Complete Response Letter (CRL) for the CTx-1301 (dexmethylphenidate HCl) NDA. The CRL identified specific requests for additional CMC information and did not identify any concerns regarding the clinical safety or efficacy of CTx-1301, the Company’s lead ADHD asset.

Since then, Cingulate and its contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO), Bend Bioscience, have substantially completed the manufacturing work required to address the CMC requests in the CRL and are finalizing the supporting data and documentation for resubmission. As announced on November 9, 2026, the Company expects to resubmit the NDA between December 2026 and January 2027. After the FDA receives the resubmission, it is expected to classify it as a Class 1 or Class 2 resubmission, which carry review goals of two and six months, respectively.

Third Quarter Financial Results

Cash and Working Capital: As of September 30, 2026, Cingulate had approximately $23.2 million in cash and cash equivalents, compared to $11.0 million as of December 31, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by capital raised during the first nine months of 2026, including the close of a $12.0 million private placement in the first quarter and $22.5 million of capital raised on Cingulate’s At-the-Market Agreement with AGP and Purchase Agreement with Lincoln Park Capital, partially offset by $20.4 million in cash used for operations. As of September 30, 2026, Cingulate had approximately $18.8 million in working capital, an increase of $16.1 million as compared to December 31, 2025.

Under its current business plan, the Company believes its cash and cash equivalents will be sufficient to fund operations into mid-2027, including costs associated with seeking regulatory approval for CTx-1301, and continuing the build-out of commercial readiness capabilities.

R&D Expenses: Research and development expenses were $2.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of 2.2% from $2.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, driven primarily by higher drug manufacturing costs to address the CMC information requested in the FDA’s CRL, partially offset by lower clinical operations costs following the conclusion of clinical study activities in early 2025, the absence of regulatory costs incurred in the prior-year period in connection with preparing the CTx-1301 NDA, and lower personnel expenses. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, R&D expenses were $6.6 million, a decrease of 15.3% from $7.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, driven primarily by lower clinical operations and regulatory costs, partially offset by increased manufacturing activities related to CTx-1301 following the CRL.

SG&A Expenses: Selling, general and administrative expenses (SG&A) were $4.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $3.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of 45.5%. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, SG&A expenses were $14.2 million, compared to $6.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of 116.6%. The increases were driven primarily by the build-out of commercial readiness capabilities, including increased headcount and expanded market access, pricing, reimbursement and medical affairs activity conducted through Indegene, the Company’s commercialization partner.

Net Loss: Net loss was $7.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $7.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net loss was $22.9 million, compared to $16.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increases primarily reflect the higher SG&A expenses described above, partially offset in the third quarter by a smaller loss from the change in fair value of derivative and lower interest expense, and for the nine-month period by lower R&D expenses.

About Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)

ADHD is a chronic neurobiological and developmental disorder that affects millions of children and often continues into adulthood. The estimated market size of the US ADHD market is approximately 100 million annual prescriptions. The condition is marked by an ongoing pattern of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity that interferes with functioning or development. In the U.S., over 20 million patients have been diagnosed with ADHD. Among this group, 12 million are adults and over 8 million are under the age of 17. According to the CDC, just 53.6 percent of all children and teens with ADHD reported they were actively treating their symptoms with medication in 2022, with 65-90 percent demonstrating clinical ADHD symptoms that persist into adulthood. Current market trends demonstrate that adult ADHD prevalence is larger and growing faster than the child and adolescent segments combined.

About CTx-1301

CTx-1301 (dexmethylphenidate HCl) is a once-daily, multi-core tablet utilizing Cingulate’s proprietary Precision Timed Release™ (PTR™) platform to deliver three precisely timed releases of active medication across the day. This design aims to provide rapid onset of effect and entire active-day duration. CTx-1301 is being evaluated for the treatment of ADHD under the FDA’s 505(b)(2) pathway. In October 2025, the FDA accepted for review the NDA for CTx-1301 and assigned a PDUFA target action date of May 31, 2026. On June 1, 2026, the FDA issued a Complete Response Letter for the CTx-1301 NDA; the Company and its CDMO have since substantially completed the manufacturing work required to address the CMC requests, and the Company expects to resubmit the NDA between December 2026 and January 2026. There can be no assurance regarding the timing of any resubmission or whether approval will occur.

About Precision Timed Release™ (PTR™) Platform Technology

Cingulate is developing ADHD and anxiety disorder product candidates capable of achieving true once-daily dosing using Cingulate’s innovative PTR drug delivery platform technology. It incorporates a proprietary Erosion Barrier Layer (EBL) providing control of drug release at precise, pre-defined times with no release of drug prior to the intended release. The EBL technology is enrobed around a drug-containing core to give a tablet-in-tablet dose form. It is designed to erode at a controlled rate until eventually the drug is released from the core tablet. The EBL formulation, Oralogik™, is licensed from BDD Pharma. Cingulate intends to utilize its PTR technology to expand and augment its clinical-stage pipeline by identifying and developing additional product candidates in other therapeutic areas in addition to Anxiety and ADHD.

About Cingulate Inc.

Cingulate Inc. (NASDAQ: CING) is a biopharmaceutical company utilizing its proprietary PTR drug delivery platform technology to build and advance a pipeline of next-generation pharmaceutical products, designed to improve the lives of patients suffering from frequently diagnosed conditions characterized by burdensome daily dosing regimens and suboptimal treatment outcomes. With an initial focus on the treatment of ADHD, Cingulate is identifying and evaluating additional therapeutic areas where PTR technology may be employed to develop future product candidates, including to treat anxiety disorders. Cingulate is headquartered in Kansas City. For more information, visit Cingulate.com.

TORONTO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Chemtrade Logistics Income Fund (TSX: CHE.UN, OTCQX®: CGIFF) (“Chemtrade” or the “Fund”) today announced results for the three and nine-month period ended September 30, 2026. The financial statements and MD&A will be available on Chemtrade’s website at www.chemtradelogistics.com and on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.com.

Third Quarter 2026 Highlights

  • Revenue of $633.1 million, an increase of $100.4 million or 18.8% year-over-year. Excluding the impact of foreign exchange, revenue for 2026 was $92.9 million higher than 2025, driven by higher selling prices for merchant acid, sulphur products and Regen acid in the ASP segment as well as revenue related to the Polytec acquisition in the WS segment. This more than offset lower selling prices for chlor-alkali products and lower volumes of sodium chlorate in the EC segment.
  • Adjusted EBITDA(1) of $145.1 million, a decrease of $6.1 million or 4.0% year-over-year; excluding the impact of foreign exchange, Adjusted EBITDA was $8.3 million lower than 2025. Adjusted EBITDA from the Polytec acquisition, lower corporate costs and higher Adjusted EBITDA for sulphur products were not sufficient to offset lower selling prices for chlor-alkali products and lower volumes of sodium chlorate. Adjusted EBITDA for water products was also lower as higher selling prices did not fully offset higher input costs.
  • Net earnings of $47.3 million, an increase of $5.0 million year-over-year primarily due to lower finance costs partially offset by lower Adjusted EBITDA, higher income tax expense and higher depreciation and amortization expense.
  • Cash flows from operating activities of $156.1 million, an increase of $5.9 million or 3.9% year-over-year, mainly due to decreases in working capital and interest paid compared to 2025, partially offset by lower Adjusted EBITDA.
  • Distributable cash after maintenance capital expenditures(1) of $75.7 million, a decrease of $2.1 million or 2.7% year-over-year reflecting lower Adjusted EBITDA, partially offset by lower maintenance capital expenditures(1). Distributable cash after maintenance capital expenditures per unit(1) of $0.68 was $0.01 lower year-over-year.
  • During the first quarter of 2026, Chemtrade increased its monthly distribution by approximately 4% to $0.06 per unit or $0.72 per unit per year. Chemtrade’s Payout ratio(1) for the third quarter of 2026 was 27% and for the last twelve months was 46%.
  • During the third quarter of 2026, Chemtrade purchased approximately 1.0 million units as part of its normal course issuer bid (NCIB). Under its current NCIB, which terminates on April 16, 2027, Chemtrade is authorized to purchase approximately 5.8 million units of which approximately 3.6 million remain available for purchase as of November 10, 2026.
  • Chemtrade continues to maintain a prudent balance sheet, with a Net debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA(1) ratio of 2.48x at the end of the third quarter of 2026.
  • Due to geopolitical events, several of Chemtrade’s key products and raw material inputs have seen significant price volatility during 2026. Despite this volatility, Chemtrade’s 2026 Adjusted EBITDA expectations continue to be largely in line with the guidance issued at the beginning of the year but now within a tighter range of $495.0 to $515.0 million.
  • After a comprehensive request for proposal process for external audit services, the Fund’s Board of Trustees has approved the appointment of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as the Fund’s external auditor for fiscal 2027. KPMG LLP will continue to serve as the Fund’s external auditor through the financial year ending December 31, 2026.

(1) Adjusted EBITDA is a Total of Segments measure, Distributable cash after maintenance capital expenditures is a non-IFRS measure and Net debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA, Distributable cash after maintenance and capital expenditures per unit and Payout ratio are non-IFRS ratios. Maintenance capital expenditures is a Supplementary financial measure. Please see Non-IFRS and Other Financial Measures for more information.

Scott Rook, President and CEO of Chemtrade, commented, “Our third quarter results reflected a continuation of the trends of the second quarter as the stability of the ASP and WS segments was offset by the softness of EC, particularly in chlor-alkali. However, our diversified product mix, operational excellence, and exceptional team continue to demonstrate resilience and to deliver strong results.”

Sulphur costs remained at historically high levels in the third quarter. Our ASP segment is largely insulated from sulphur price changes, but higher costs have been a headwind in WS despite our team being able to offset more than 80% of cost increases through pricing adjustments this year. There are signs that sulphur costs are starting to ease as demonstrated by fourth quarter sulphur settling 13% below the third quarter, which is expected to support WS margins. With 2026 nearly complete, we expect a substantial improvement in the fourth quarter over the same period in 2025. I would like to thank our entire team for the dedication and agility that position Chemtrade to deliver near-record annual results despite challenging market conditions,” continued Mr. Rook.

“We remain committed to the growth targets in our Vision 2030 strategic framework, supported by our strong balance sheet. We ended the quarter at our target leverage, and for the right inorganic growth opportunity we are prepared to let it rise modestly into the higher 2x range.”

“Over the past few years, Chemtrade has transformed through reliability, productivity improvements, pricing discipline and organic growth investments. We intend to continue the transformation by converting from an income trust to a corporation, which we believe will, among other benefits, broaden our investor base. Subject to Board approval, we expect to continue our balanced approach to capital allocation: eligible dividends, share repurchases under our active NCIB, and growth investments. We urge our unitholders to vote in favour of the conversion,” concluded Mr. Rook.

Consolidated Financial Summary of Q3 2026

The Canadian dollar weakened by $0.02 relative to the U.S. dollar during the third quarter of 2026 compared with the third quarter of 2025, contributing positively to consolidated revenue and consolidated Adjusted EBITDA by $7.5 million and $2.2 million, respectively.

Revenue for the third quarter of 2026 was $633.1 million, an increase of $100.4 or 18.8% year-over-year. Excluding the impact of foreign exchange, revenue was $92.9 million higher than the prior year period. The increase was due to (i) higher selling prices for merchant acid, sulphur products, and Regen acid in the ASP segment; and (ii) revenue from the acquisition of Polytec as well as higher selling prices for water solutions products in the WS segment. These gains were partially offset by (i) lower volumes of sodium chlorate in the EC segment; and (ii) lower MECU netbacks for chlor-alkali products partially offset by higher volumes in the EC segment.

Adjusted EBITDA was $145.1 million, a decrease of $6.1 million or 4.0% year-over-year. Excluding the impact of foreign exchange, Adjusted EBITDA was $8.3 million lower than the prior year period. The decrease was primarily due to (i) lower MECU netbacks for chlor-alkali products as well as lower sales volumes for sodium chlorate in the EC segment; and (ii) lower margins for water solutions products in the WS segment. A partial offset was provided by (i) lower corporate costs; (ii) Adjusted EBITDA contribution from the Polytec acquisition in the WS segment; and (iii) higher Adjusted EBITDA for sulphur products in the ASP segment.

Distributable cash after maintenance capital expenditures for the third quarter of 2026 was $75.7 million or $0.68 per unit, compared with $77.8 million or $0.69 per unit in the third quarter of 2025. The year-over year change primarily reflects lower Adjusted EBITDA, partially offset by lower maintenance capital expenditures and a lower number of units. Chemtrade’s payout ratio for the twelve months ended September 30, 2026 was 46%.

The timing of maintenance capex in 2026 is significantly different than 2025. During 2025, approximately one-third of the annual maintenance capex was incurred during the fourth quarter, whereas less than one-third is expected to be incurred in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Chemtrade maintained a strong balance sheet through the third quarter of 2026. As of September 30, 2026, Chemtrade’s Net debt was $1.2 billion and its Net Debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA ratio was 2.48x. As of the end of the third quarter of 2026, Chemtrade also maintained ample financial liquidity with approximately $461 million (US$324 million) undrawn on its credit facilities, in addition to $55.7 million of cash on hand.

Segmented Financial Summary of Q3 2026

As of 2026, Chemtrade has separated the former Sulphur and Water Chemicals (SWC) segment into two new segments, the Acid and Sulphur Products (ASP) segment and the Water Solutions (WS) segment. Chemtrade now reports its results in three segments:

  • The ASP segment markets, removes, and/or produces merchant, Regen, and ultrapure acid, sodium nitrite, all other sulphur-related products, and provides other processing services.
  • The WS, segment manufactures and markets a variety of inorganic coagulants used in water treatment, including aluminum sulphate (alum), aluminum chlorohydrate (ACH), polyaluminum chloride (PACl), and ferric sulphate (ferric). WS also provides value-added water solutions.
  • The Electrochemicals (EC), segment manufactures and markets sodium chlorate and chlor-alkali products including caustic soda, chlorine and hydrochloric acid, largely for the pulp and paper, oil and gas, and water treatment industries. These products are marketed primarily to North American and South American customers.

The ASP segment reported revenue of $231.1 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $176.9 million for the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA in the ASP segment was $52.7 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $51.1 million for the third quarter of 2025. The weaker Canadian dollar relative to the U.S. dollar during the third quarter of 2026 compared with the third quarter of 2025 had a positive impact on ASP revenue and ASP Adjusted EBITDA of $3.2 million and $0.7 million, respectively.

Excluding the impact of foreign exchange, as noted above, ASP revenue in the third quarter of 2026 increased by $51.0 million or 28.8% year-over-year. The increase in comparable ASP revenue was primarily due to higher selling prices for merchant acid, sulphur products, and Regen acid. Excluding the impact of foreign exchange, as noted above, ASP Adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter of 2026 increased by $0.9 million or 1.8% year-over-year. The increase in comparable ASP Adjusted EBITDA was primarily due to higher Adjusted EBITDA for sulphur products.

The WS segment reported revenue of $210.4 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $157.2 million for the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA in the WS segment was $40.1 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $41.1 million for the third quarter of 2025. The weaker Canadian dollar relative to the U.S. dollar during the third quarter of 2026 had a positive year-over-year impact on WS revenue and WS Adjusted EBITDA of $2.5 million and $0.2 million, respectively.

Excluding the impact of foreign exchange, as noted above, WS revenue in the third quarter of 2026 increased by $50.7 million or 32.3% year-over-year. The increase in WS revenue was primarily due to additional revenue from the Polytec acquisition and higher selling prices for water solutions products. Excluding the impact of foreign exchange, as noted above, WS Adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter of 2026 decreased by $1.2 million or 2.9% year-over-year. The decrease in comparable WS Adjusted EBITDA was primarily due to lower margins for water solutions products partially offset by additional Adjusted EBITDA from the Polytec acquisition. Higher selling prices for water solutions products offset approximately 80% of the higher input costs.

The EC segment reported revenue of $191.6 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $198.6 million for the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA in the EC segment was $74.7 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $93.8 million for the third quarter of 2025. The weaker Canadian dollar relative to the U.S. dollar during the third quarter of 2026 had a positive year-over-year impact on EC revenue and EC Adjusted EBITDA of $1.8 million and $1.4 million, respectively.

Excluding the impact of foreign exchange, as noted above, EC revenue in the third quarter of 2026 was $8.8 million or 4.4% lower compared to the third quarter of 2025. The decrease in EC revenue was primarily due to (i) lower MECU netbacks for chlor-alkali products, partially offset by higher volumes; and (ii) lower volumes for sodium chlorate. MECU netbacks decreased by approximately $260 year-over-year with approximately 95% of the decline attributable to hydrochloric acid and chlorine. Excluding the impact of foreign exchange, as noted above, EC Adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026 was $20.5 million or 21.9% lower year-over-year due to (i) lower MECU netbacks for chlor-alkali products; and (ii) lower volumes for sodium chlorate.

Corporate costs for the third quarter of 2026 were $22.4 million, compared with $34.8 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease in corporate costs was primarily due to (i) $9.5 million of lower long-term incentive compensation costs; (ii) $2.5 million of lower short-term incentive compensation costs; and (iii) $2.0 million of legal and other costs in 2025 related to the Polytec acquisition. Higher realized foreign exchange losses of $0.8 million were a partial offset.

2026 Guidance

Due to geopolitical events, several of Chemtrade’s key products and raw material inputs have seen significant price volatility during 2026. Despite this volatility, Chemtrade’s 2026 Adjusted EBITDA expectations continue to be largely in line with the guidance issued at the beginning of the year but now within a tighter range of $495.0 to $515.0 million. Based on current guidance assumptions, including the anticipated spending on Growth capital expenditures and changes in capital allocation, Chemtrade expects to end 2026 with a Net debt to Adjusted EBITDA ratio of close to 2.5x and an implied Payout ratio of approximately 40%.

At the midpoint of this guidance range, Chemtrade’s Adjusted EBITDA for 2026 would be comparable to the historically high level achieved in 2025, highlighting the significant step-change in Chemtrade’s Adjusted EBITDA and cashflow generation in the last five years

The timing of maintenance capex in 2026 is significantly different than 2025. During 2025, approximately one-third of the annual maintenance capex was incurred during the fourth quarter, whereas less than one-third is expected to be incurred in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Chemtrade Vision 2030

In May 2025, Chemtrade shared Chemtrade Vision 2030 where one of the key aspects is to grow mid-cycle annual Adjusted EBITDA to between $550.0 million and $600.0 million by 2030. Chemtrade expects to achieve this target by continuing to focus on operational and commercial excellence while pursuing both organic and external growth opportunities such as the acquisitions of Polytec and the assets of Thatcher Group in 2025. This improvement in Adjusted EBITDA, alongside Chemtrade’s commitment to returning capital to unitholders while maintaining a prudent balance sheet, is expected to deliver compelling value on a per unit basis.

Update on Organic Growth Projects

Chemtrade remains focused on its long-term objective of delivering sustained earnings growth and generating value for investors. To accomplish this, Chemtrade has identified various organic growth initiatives. In 2026, Chemtrade plans to invest between $35.0 million and $45.0 million in growth capital expenditures with a focus on water treatment chemicals projects.

In Ultrapure Acid, following quality improvement upgrades and plant start-ups at the Cairo, Ohio and Tulsa, Oklahoma facilities, Chemtrade has been qualified and supplying commercially to two customers while actively progressing through certification with two other customers. Chemtrade remains on track to achieve its targets in UPA.

Distributions and Capital Allocation Update

Distributions declared in the third quarter of 2026 totalled $0.18 per unit, comprised of monthly distributions of $0.06 per unit, which reflect a 4% increase beginning with the distribution declared during the month of January 2026. The distribution is well-covered by Chemtrade’s robust cash flow generation with a third quarter 2026 payout ratio of 27% and a last twelve months payout ratio of 46%.

During the third quarter of 2026, Chemtrade purchased approximately 1.0 million units as part of its normal course issuer bid (NCIB) that terminates in April 2027 and authorizes Chemtrade to purchase approximately 5.8 million units. As of November 10th, 2026, approximately 3.6 million units remain available for purchase. Purchases of units are effected through the facilities of the TSX and/or alternative Canadian trading systems and are made by means of open market transactions, or such other means as may be permitted by the TSX, including block purchases of units, at prevailing market rates. The timing and amount of any purchases are subject to management’s discretion.

Chemtrade’s management and Board of Trustees continue to assess opportunities to further adjust and optimize its capital structure. Subsequent to September 30, 2026, Chemtrade took steps to optimize its balance sheet and liquidity as outlined in this press release and third quarter financial disclosures.

Rohit Bhardwaj, CFO of Chemtrade, commented on Chemtrade’s financial position and capital allocation, “Despite the uncertain and volatile macroeconomic backdrop, Chemtrade maintains a prudent balance sheet and continues to act on opportunities that improve its financial position. To that effect, subsequent to the end of the third quarter, we issued $200 million of 5.75% senior unsecured notes that mature in 2032 while extending and upsizing our credit facility.

We exited Q3 2026 with on-target leverage of 2.5x Net Debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA, which provides the financial flexibility to execute on various growth strategies as they may arise. Although we may allow a slightly above target leverage for a short period of time, the upper bound remains in the high 2x range. Our disciplined capital allocation strategy is designed to provide a healthy balance of debt reduction, sustainable earnings growth, and returning of capital to unitholders via the NCIB and (eligible) dividends should our proposed conversion to a corporation achieve unitholder approval later in 2026,” concluded Mr. Bhardwaj.

Senior unsecured notes maturing October 1, 2032

On October 20, 2026, Chemtrade closed the private placement of $200.0 million aggregate principal notes (“the “Notes”) via the reopening of the 5.75% senior unsecured notes maturing October 1, 2032. The Notes were issued at a price of $982.50 per $1,000 principal amount (yield of 6.104%), plus accrued interest from and including October 1, 2026. The Notes have identical terms (except for their date of issue and issuance price) as, and form part of a single series with, the $250.0 million aggregate principal amount of 5.750% Senior Unsecured Notes due 2032 issued by the Company on October 1, 2025, resulting in an aggregate of $450.0 million principal amount outstanding of 5.750% Senior Unsecured Notes due 2032. The net proceeds of the offering were used to reduce indebtedness and for general corporate purposes.

Extension of Credit Facility

Subsequent to September 30, 2026, Chemtrade extended and upsized its credit facility. The updated credit facility has a limit of US$700.0 million (from US$600.0 million prior) and a maturity date of November 9, 2031 (from October 31, 2030 prior).

Trust Conversion

On October 9, 2026, Chemtrade announced a proposed conversion of the Fund from an income trust to a corporate structure pursuant to a court-approved statutory plan of arrangement (the “Plan”), and subject to the terms and conditions set forth in an arrangement agreement entered into between the Fund and Chemtrade Inc. (“PubCo”) dated October 9, 2026 (the “Arrangement Agreement”).

On November 3, 2026, the Fund obtained an interim order (the “Interim Order”) from the Ontario Superior Court of Justice (Commercial List) in respect of the Plan, authorizing, among other things, the calling and holding of a special meeting of Unitholders (the “Special Meeting”) to consider and vote on the Plan.

Complete details of the terms of the Plan and a copy of the Arrangement Agreement will be provided in an information circular (the “Meeting Circular”) to Unitholders entitled to receive notice of and vote at the Special Meeting. The Meeting Circular will be mailed to entitled Unitholders and will be made available and filed on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca as well as on Chemtrade’s Investor Relations section of its website at www.chemtradelogistics.com/investors, on or about November 16, 2026. Unitholders are strongly urged to review and evaluate the information in the Meeting Circular once received or accessed.

The Plan will be subject to Unitholder approval at the Special Meeting, expected to be held on December 7, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. (Eastern Standard Time). The Plan must be approved by at least 66 2/3% of the votes cast by Unitholders voting in person or by proxy at the Special Meeting.

Change in Auditors

After a comprehensive request for proposal (“RFP”) process for external audit services, the Fund’s Board of Trustees has approved the appointment of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP (“PwC”) as the Fund’s external auditor for fiscal 2027. KPMG LLP (“KPMG”) will continue to serve as the Fund’s external auditor through the financial year ending December 31, 2026.

Consistent with Fund’s commitment to strong governance and oversight, the Audit Committee of the Board of Trustees initiated the RFP in recognition of KPMG’s long tenure as the Fund’s external auditor. Following a thorough evaluation, the Board of Trustees, on the recommendation of the Audit Committee, selected PwC on the basis of its depth of expertise, qualifications, and independence.

The Fund thanks KPMG for its 26 years of service as the Fund’s auditor and for the valuable insight and professional stewardship it has provided over that time.

At the Fund’s request, KPMG will resign as external auditor effective on the first business day following the filing of the Fund’s audited consolidated financial statements for the year ending December 31, 2026 and KPMG’s auditor’s report thereon. PwC will be appointed on the same day to fill the resulting vacancy and will hold office until the Fund’s 2027 annual meeting of unitholders, at which the Fund intends to propose the appointment of PwC as external auditor for the ensuing year.

There have been no modified opinions in KPMG’s reports on the Fund’s financial statements for the two most recently completed fiscal years, and in the opinion of the Fund there have been no “reportable events” (as defined in National Instrument 51-102 – Continuous Disclosure Obligations) between the Fund and KPMG. The Fund’s Notice of Change of Auditor, together with the letters from KPMG and PwC, will be filed on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

About Chemtrade

Chemtrade operates a diversified business providing industrial chemicals and services to customers in North and South America. Chemtrade is one of North America’s largest suppliers of sulphuric acid, spent acid processing services, inorganic coagulants for water treatment, sodium chlorate, sodium nitrite and sodium hydrosulphite. Chemtrade is also a leading producer of high purity sulphuric acid for the semiconductor industry in North America. Chemtrade is a leading regional supplier of sulphur, chlor-alkali products, and zinc oxide. Additionally, Chemtrade provides value-added water solutions, as well as industrial services such as processing by-products and waste streams.

NON-IFRS AND OTHER FINANCIAL MEASURES

Non-IFRS financial measures and non-IFRS ratios

Non-IFRS financial measures are financial measures disclosed by an entity that (a) depict historical or expected future financial performance, financial position or cash flow of an entity, (b) with respect to their composition, exclude amounts that are included in, or include amounts that are excluded from, the composition of the most directly comparable financial measure disclosed in the primary financial statements of the entity, (c) are not disclosed in the financial statements of the entity and (d) are not a ratio, fraction, percentage or similar representation. Non-IFRS ratios are financial measures disclosed by an entity that are in the form of a ratio, fraction, percentage, or similar representation that has a non-IFRS financial measure as one or more of its components, and that are not disclosed in the financial statements of the entity.

These non-IFRS financial measures and non-IFRS ratios are not standardized financial measures under IFRS and, therefore, are unlikely to be comparable to similar financial measures presented by other entities. Management believes these non-IFRS financial measures and non-IFRS ratios provide transparent and useful supplemental information to help investors evaluate Chemtrade’s financial performance, financial condition and liquidity using the same measures as management. CHARLOTTE, NC / ACCESS Newswire / November 13, 2026 / Air T, Inc. (NASDAQ:AIRT) is an industrious American company with a portfolio of businesses, each of which is independent yet interrelated. We seek dynamic individuals and teams to operate companies with processes and insights that drive increasing value over time. We believe we can invest corporate resources to help activate growth and overcome challenges.

Our core segments are regional airline, overnight air cargo; commercial aircraft, engines and parts; ground support equipment; digital solutions; and aviation leasing and asset management.

Today, Air T announced results for the fiscal second quarter ended September 30, 2026:

  • Revenues totaled $146.9 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $82.8 million, or 129% from the prior year's comparable quarter. Revenues for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 included $56.8 million related to our acquisition of Regional Express Holdings Pty Ltd ("Rex") completed on December 18, 2025.
  • Operating loss was $11.8 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to the prior year's comparable quarter's operating income of $5.5 million.
  • Loss before income taxes was $16.2 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to income before income taxes of $7.2 million in the prior year's comparable quarter.
  • Adjusted EBITDA* was $4.4 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $7.9 million in the prior year's comparable quarter.
  • The investment balance for the Company's equity method investees was $26.2 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $27.9 million at September 30, 2025.
  • Net loss per share was $7.48 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to net income per share of $1.61 in the prior year's comparable quarter.

*Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial measure; see below for further explanation and reconciliation to GAAP measure.

Company Chairman and CEO Nick Swenson commented:

"While focused in one sector and with some interdependencies, Air T can be viewed as a set of businesses that operate independently of one another. The quarter just passed is an example of widely variable operational dynamics across our businesses. Several of our businesses, including Crestone and GGS, performed quite well in absolute terms and against comparables in the quarter. Crestone has particularly strong momentum at the moment. Rex financial performance was notably challenged in the quarter due to a combination of unscheduled engine removals, delays at engine overhaul shops and a doubling of fuel costs compared to pre-war levels. Adding back the large quarterly depreciation expense at Rex, we see an Adjusted EBITDA loss of approximately $0.9 million on $56.8 million of revenues for the quarter. Management continues to support business leaders as they navigate areas of risk management and growth management."

Business Segment Results

Regional Airline

  • This segment provides scheduled regional passenger and cargo airline services in Australia, operating a fleet of aircraft serving regional communities and connecting passengers to major metropolitan centers.
  • Revenues for this segment were $56.8 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, representing a full quarter of Rex operations, which was acquired on December 18, 2025. There is no prior-year comparable. Revenue consisted of passenger revenue, ancillary fees, freight and charter, and government subsidy income.
  • Adjusted EBITDA* loss for this segment was $0.9 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. The significant add-backs to this segment's operating loss of $10.0 million include $9.4 million of depreciation and amortization. Fuel expense continued to be the primary driver of the loss, with the increase driven principally by higher per-liter fuel prices rather than increased consumption. Rex does not hedge its fuel price or related Australian dollar/U.S. dollar exposure and purchases fuel at prevailing market prices, mitigating higher costs through fare adjustments, capacity management, and fuel levy arrangements with certain state governments. Higher unscheduled engine removals, together with lower engine throughput from third-party maintenance, repair and overhaul providers, also contributed to the loss by reducing the number of aircraft available for service below planned levels.

Overnight Air Cargo

  • This segment provides air express delivery services, primarily for FedEx Corporation, and repair services.
  • Revenues for this segment totaled $34.5 million period ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $3.5 million compared to the second quarter of the prior fiscal year. The increase was principally attributable to higher pricing on flight administrative fees and billable labor at Mountain Air Cargo ("MAC").
  • Adjusted EBITDA* for this segment was $2.6 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $0.8 million when compared to the prior year's comparable quarter. The increase was mainly driven by higher revenue. In addition, higher gross margins related to both flight operations and maintenance at MAC drove operating income and Adjusted EBITDA higher.

Commercial Aircraft, Engines and Parts

  • This segment acquires, leases, manages, repairs, disassembles, and sells commercial aircraft, jet engines, and aviation components, and provides related asset management, procurement, overhaul, repair, and logistics services.
  • Revenues for this segment totaled $28.5 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $7.0 million from the comparable prior year quarter. The increase was largely attributable to increased component sales at Contrail, primarily driven by an increase in sales to a single customer. Landing Gear Support Services, Inc. ("LGSS") and AirCo also contributed to the revenue growth due to strategic investments in aircraft inventory that were not in place during the prior year comparable quarter. Jet Yard saw reduced revenue, primarily due to the prior year quarter's revenue including some larger projects that did not recur in the current quarter.
  • Adjusted EBITDA* for this segment was $1.5 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to adjusted EBITDA* of $6.9 million in the prior year's comparable quarter. The decrease was primarily attributable to a $7.0 million gain on sale of aircraft in the prior year quarter, which did not recur in the current quarter. Partially offsetting the impact of this transaction was the overall revenue increase in this segment.

Ground Support Equipment

  • This segment-which includes some of the world-leading offerings in the category-manufactures, repairs, and maintains mobile deicers and other specialized ground-support equipment. Customers include passenger and cargo airlines, airports, the military, and other industrial customers.
  • Revenues for this segment totaled $18.9 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $9.2 million from $9.6 million in the prior year's comparable quarter. The increase was primarily driven by a higher number of deicing trucks sold in the current quarter as a result of timing on fulfilling annual orders for a large customer.
  • Adjusted EBITDA* for this segment was $2.7 million in the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to adjusted EBITDA* of $1.7 million in the prior year's comparable quarter. The increase was primarily attributable to the higher sales from timing of revenues as noted above.
  • At September 30, 2026, this segment's order backlog was $11.6 million compared to $12.9 million at September 30, 2025.

Digital Solutions

  • This segment develops and provides digital aviation and other business services to customers within the aviation industry to generate recurring subscription revenues.
  • The digital solutions segment contributed $2.6 million of revenues for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $2.2 million in the prior year's comparable quarter. The increase of $0.4 million was primarily due to continued growth in data analytics and airspace management engagements.
  • Adjusted EBITDA* for this segment was $0.1 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $0.2 million from the prior year's comparable quarter. The improvement was primarily driven by two factors: revenue growth at high incremental margins and lower labor costs as AI-driven tools improved efficiency.

Aviation Leasing and Asset Management

  • This segment originates and structures asset acquisitions and related financings and provides lease administration, technical and risk management, and remarketing services for aircraft and engines on lease to airline customers globally.
  • The aviation leasing and asset management segment revenues totaled $7.8 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, representing a full quarter of activity for Crestone and Arena, which made up the segment as of the acquisition of Arena on June 10, 2026. There is no prior year comparable quarter. Revenue consisted of origination, due diligence, disposition, and asset management fees.
  • Adjusted EBITDA* for this segment was $1.3 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, representing a full quarter of operations after the Arena acquisition and quarter-to-date activity related to Crestone Air Partners. The largest reconciling items between Adjusted EBITDA and this segment's operating loss of $4.7 million include an unfavorable earnout remeasurement of $3.3 million, depreciation and amortization add-backs of $2.2 million, and post-acquisition integration costs of $0.5 million.
